edges.description: Host entry gives B. quintana access to the bloodstream, where Bartonella Trw type IV secretion machinery supports erythrocyte tropism.
Intraerythrocytic bacteremia produces the acute, often relapsing febrile illness that is the cardinal trench-fever syndrome.
Persistent B. quintana bacteremia can remain chronic and seed blood-culture-negative bacterial endocarditis.
The acute bacteremic illness produces high fever.
The acute syndrome produces characteristic shin (tibial) bone pain.
Persistent blood infection is the defining manifestation of this branch.
Chronic bacteremia can seed bacterial endocarditis.
Chronic B. quintana infection can produce chronic lymphadenopathy.
Circulating B. quintana adheres to vascular endothelium, the step that precedes the vasoproliferative branch.
Endothelial adherence positions B. quintana to drive the BafA/VEGF pro-angiogenic response.
Pro-angiogenic endothelial signaling is a molecular route into vasoproliferative bacillary angiomatosis.
Louse infestation in homeless, impoverished settings supplies the body-louse vector whose infectious feces inoculate B. quintana.

nodes.description: The classic trench-fever syndrome is an acute bacteremic illness with sudden headache, pain in the shins, and high fever; a relapsing form with a shorter initial period and frequent relapses (the "five-day"/quintan periodicity) was also described.

evidence.reference_title: Molecular epidemiology of bartonella infections in patients with bacillary angiomatosis-peliosis.
evidence.snippet: Of the 49 patients with bacillary angiomatosis-peliosis, 26 (53 percent) were infected with B. henselae and 23 (47 percent) with B. quintana.

nodes.description: Bartonella BafA acts as a VEGF receptor 2 ligand; the B. quintana BafA homolog is functional, supporting a homologous pro-angiogenic route into endothelial proliferation in B. quintana-associated bacillary angiomatosis.

evidence.reference_title: The Bartonella autotransporter BafA activates the host VEGF pathway to drive angiogenesis.
evidence.snippet: BafA interacts with vascular endothelial growth factor (VEGF) receptor-2 and activates the downstream signaling pathway, suggesting that BafA functions as a VEGF analog.

evidence.reference_title: The Bartonella autotransporter BafA activates the host VEGF pathway to drive angiogenesis.
evidence.snippet: A BafA homolog from a related pathogen, Bartonella quintana, is also functional.

nodes.description: B. quintana is an intracellular Bartonella pathogen; residence inside host cells constrains treatment toward cell-penetrant antimicrobials such as doxycycline.

nodes.description: The Bartonella Trw type IV secretion system contributes to host-specific adhesion to erythrocytes, supporting the long-lasting intraerythrocytic bacteremia that characterizes B. quintana infection.

evidence.reference_title: The Trw type IV secretion system of Bartonella mediates host-specific adhesion to erythrocytes.
evidence.snippet: The corresponding genes encode components of the type IV secretion system (T4SS) Trw, demonstrating that this virulence factor laterally acquired by the Bartonella lineage is directly involved in adherence to erythrocytes.

nodes.description: Variably expressed outer membrane proteins (Vomps), the trimeric autotransporter adhesins of B. quintana, mediate adherence to extracellular matrix and endothelial cells, the adhesion step upstream of the pro-angiogenic endothelial response.

evidence.reference_title: Trimeric autotransporter adhesin-dependent adherence of Bartonella henselae, Bartonella quintana, and Yersinia enterocolitica to matrix components and endothelial cells under static and dynamic flow conditions.
evidence.snippet: Under static conditions, ECM adherence of B. henselae, B. quintana, and Y. enterocolitica was strongly dependent on the expression of their particular TAAs.
